summary_html: Cases arising on **federal lands/facilities** or involving **Indian children** invoke federal/tribal jurisdictional rules (VICAA for federal facilities; **ICWA** for Indian children and tribal preference/jurisdiction).
authority_html:
- **VICAA (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — federal-facility reporting mandates  
- **ICWA (25 U.S.C. §§ 1901–1963)** — tribal jurisdiction, placement preferences, notice to tribes

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a tribe's determination that a child is a member or eligible for membership conclusively establishes the child's status as an Indian child for purposes of ICWA's adoptive placement preferences, and affirmed summary judgment.
key_cases.relevance: This is the Minnesota rule for the threshold question that triggers ICWA at all: who decides whether the child is an Indian child.
key_cases.quote: a tribal determination that a child is a member or eligible for membership in that tribe is conclusive evidence that a child is an "Indian child" under section 1915

key_cases.holding: The court held that neither ICWA nor Minnesota law authorizes transferring pre-adoptive and adoptive placement proceedings for an off-reservation Indian child to tribal court, and reversed the transfer.
key_cases.relevance: This is the Minnesota Supreme Court's controlling statement of how far ICWA's tribal-transfer right reaches for an off-reservation Indian child.
key_cases.quote: with respect to an Indian child not residing or domiciled on the child's tribe's reservation, transfer is limited to foster care placement and termination of parental rights proceedings

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of the Child of T.T.B.
key_cases.holding: The court held there was good cause under ICWA to deny transfer to tribal court because the transfer motions were not made promptly after notice and the proceedings had reached an advanced stage.
key_cases.relevance: It supplies Minnesota's good-cause standard for refusing an ICWA transfer, turning on promptness and the stage of the proceedings.
key_cases.quote: the district court had good cause to deny the motions to transfer jurisdiction of the case to the tribal court

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of Children of S.R.K.
key_cases.holding: The court held that ICWA and MIFPA require qualified expert witness testimony as part of the court's beyond-a-reasonable-doubt determination that continued parental custody is likely to cause serious emotional or physical damage, and affirmed the terminations.
key_cases.relevance: It is the controlling Minnesota Supreme Court construction of ICWA and MIFPA's evidentiary requirements once a case is identified as involving an Indian child.
key_cases.quote: The statute provides that the court's serious-damage determination must be supported by evidence "including testimony of qualified expert witnesses."

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of the Children of S.W.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination of parental rights to Indian children, holding the district court did not err in finding that active and reasonable efforts to reunify had failed and in refusing to invalidate the proceedings for earlier ICWA violations.
key_cases.relevance: It applies the ICWA and Minnesota Tribal/State Agreement definition of active efforts once a case is identified as involving Indian children.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the district court did not err by finding that active and reasonable efforts failed to reunite the family.

state_agency.name: Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the county or Tribal child protection agency where the child lives — the directory link is on dcyf.mn.gov/individuals-and-families/report-abuse

mandatory_reporters: Designated professionals only (not universal) — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1; any person may voluntarily report but is not required to (§ 260E.06, subd. 2)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in the practice of the healing arts — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)

A professional or professional's delegate engaged in social services, including employee assistance counseling and guardian ad litem and parenting time expeditor services — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1) and (b)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in hospital administration — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in psychological or psychiatric treatment — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in child care — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in education — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in correctional supervision or probation and correctional services — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in law enforcement — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A member of the clergy who received the information while engaged in ministerial duties, except information privileged under § 595.02, subd. 1(c) — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(2)

An employee or supervisor of a private or public youth recreation program (including coaching staff), as to abuse by another employee or supervisor or abuse a child discloses — Minn. Stat. § 260E.055, subd. 1(d) and subd. 2

A parent, guardian, or caretaker relying on spiritual means or prayer in lieu of medical care, when the lack of medical care may cause serious danger to the child's health — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 3

timeline_requirements.deadline: Except in a noncaregiver human trafficking assessment: immediately if sexual abuse or substantial child endangerment is alleged; within 5 calendar days for all other screened in reports
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified by statute; Minn. Stat. § 260E.20, subd. 2(b) sets the face-to-face contact deadline for the local welfare agency.
timeline_requirements.extension_grounds: Face-to-face contact on a report alleging sexual abuse or substantial child endangerment may be postponed for no more than five calendar days if the child is residing in a location confirmed to restrict contact with the alleged offender, or if the local welfare agency is pursuing a court order for the caregiver to produce the child for questioning under Minn. Stat. § 260E.22, subd. 5 (§ 260E.20, subd. 2(b)).

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified by statute; Minn. Stat. § 260E.24, subd. 1 requires the local welfare agency to conclude the assessment or investigation within 45 days.
timeline_requirements.extension_grounds: Only to complete a criminal investigation or to receive expert information requested within 45 days of receipt of the report (Minn. Stat. § 260E.24, subd. 1).
